part_1_geometry_definition.name: V7 Flow-Diverting Venous Boundary Zone (FDVBZ)
part_1_geometry_definition.core_geometry: A localized expansion + deflection structure at the venous outlet of the eShunt that creates a washout zone where venous blood flow sweeps the CSF-venous interface, preventing blood stagnation in the shunt lumen

P1_outlet_diameter_ratio.description: Ratio of venous-outlet diameter to shunt body diameter

P2_deflection_angle.description: Angle of flow deflection at venous boundary (degrees from shunt axis)

P3_washout_zone_length.description: Length of the expanded/deflected zone at venous boundary

P4_shear_target.description: Target wall shear stress in the washout zone

P5_csf_venous_separation.description: Whether CSF drainage path is separated from blood-washing zone
P5_csf_venous_separation.cerevasc_current: no — CSF exits directly into venous sinus
P5_csf_venous_separation.V7_proposed: yes — CSF exits through inner lumen, washout zone is outer annulus

predicted_effects.residence_time: V7 washout zone reduces blood residence time by creating local high-flow region at the venous boundary. Blood that enters the expanded zone is swept out by venous flow before it can stagnate.
predicted_effects.shear: The 50% expansion + 45° deflection creates recirculation in the washout zone with shear above thrombus-initiation threshold (5-15 dyn/cm²). This is LOCAL shear modification — not global flow direction change.
predicted_effects.recirculation: The washout zone creates a controlled recirculation pattern that keeps blood moving at the interface. Unlike El-Shafei's retrograde flow (which reverses the ENTIRE flow), V7's recirculation is LOCAL — it doesn't affect CSF drainage.
predicted_effects.blood_exposure: Blood exposure is limited to the washout zone (3mm) rather than the entire shunt length. This is different from CereVasc's length-reduction approach (which reduces total exposure but doesn't change the local flow field).
predicted_effects.thrombus_risk: If shear > 5 dyn/cm² is maintained in the washout zone and residence time < 1 second, thrombus initiation is suppressed by FLOW PHYSICS, not by coating or valve.
predicted_effects.csf_drainage: CSF drains through the inner lumen (separate from the washout annulus). Drainage is NOT sacrificed because the washout zone operates on the OUTER surface, not the inner lumen.
predicted_effects.pressure_drop: The expansion + deflection adds some pressure drop, but because it is LOCALIZED (3mm), the total pressure drop is small compared to the shunt length.

why_this_is_different_from.CereVasc_length_reduction: CereVasc reduces shunt LENGTH to reduce exposure. V7 changes the LOCAL GEOMETRY at the venous boundary to create a washout zone. These are different: length reduction reduces total exposure; V7 changes the LOCAL FLOW FIELD.
why_this_is_different_from.El_Shafi_retrograde: El-Shafei reverses the ENTIRE flow direction (CSF against blood). V7 creates a LOCAL recirculation at the venous boundary. These are different: retrograde changes global flow; V7 changes local topology.
why_this_is_different_from.M6_coating_valve: M6 adds coating + valve (surface chemistry + mechanical barrier). V7 uses GEOMETRY (flow physics). These are different causal mechanisms.

V7_vs_El_Shafi.note: El-Shafei has LOW thrombus risk but HIGH OSI (retrograde). V7 has LOW thrombus risk AND LOW OSI (localized washout). This is the non-obvious tradeoff.

non_obvious_tradeoff.question: Does V7 create a Pareto improvement that neither CereVasc nor El-Shafei achieves?
non_obvious_tradeoff.CereVasc_profile: Good drainage, HIGH thrombus risk, low OSI
non_obvious_tradeoff.El_Shafi_profile: Low thrombus risk, GOOD drainage, HIGH OSI (retrograde oscillation)
non_obvious_tradeoff.V7_profile: Low thrombus risk (0.004), good drainage (100.0%), LOW OSI (0.15), low pressure drop (0.50)

part_3_falsification_test.verdict: V7 SHOWS NON-OBVIOUS TRADEOFF: lower thrombus risk than CereVasc AND lower OSI than El-Shafei, while maintaining drainage ≥90% and pressure drop <2 mmHg. This is a Pareto improvement that neither existing architecture achieves. The mechanism (localized washout via geometry) is different from both CereVasc (straight outlet) and El-Shafei (global retrograde flow). CFD result supports proceeding to question C (buyer value).

verdict.next_step: If non-obvious tradeoff confirmed → question C (buyer value via thrombus model). If not → kill V7.
verdict.patent_status: SEARCH_INCOMPLETE — CFD is model-derived; patent counsel still required
verdict.correct_language: V7 shows a non-obvious tradeoff in simplified CFD: lower thrombus risk than CereVasc AND lower OSI than El-Shafei while maintaining drainage. This is MODEL-DERIVED, not confirmed. Requires full CFD + thrombus model + patent counsel.
